The primary subject is persona prompt composition from the instruction root, active persona, working-root policy, mode, and tool surface.
Prompt/persona composition is owned by Chirality, not by SDK defaults or vendor-specific product semantics.
The composer reads release-managed instruction-root governance and selected agents/AGENT_<persona>.md content; ordinary execution must not mutate the instruction root.
Prompt composition includes the working-root summary/policy while preserving instruction-root/working-root separation.
UI aliases map to canonical agents: HELP->HELP_HUMAN, ORCHESTRATE->ORCHESTRATOR, AGGREGATE->AGGREGATION, RECONCILING->RECONCILIATION, AGENTS->HELPS_HUMANS.

The boot fingerprint should include hashes for persona content, governance preface, mode, SDK tool names/versions, permission-policy version, settings-source posture, MCP server versions, and subagent policy version.
docs/PRD.md has a HASH_MISMATCH in _REFERENCES.md; PRD-derived details require confirmation against an accepted snapshot before being treated as final project truth.
Persona fallback is request/session persona, then HELP_HUMAN or configured default; other option fallback chains are owned by adjacent SDK-options work.
Prompt text is not a sufficient reliance boundary; permission, path, hook, and tool enforcement remain runtime code responsibilities.
The composer must not depend on ambient SDK settings; shipped SDK options use settingSources: [] outside this deliverable's implementation responsibility.

DEL-04-04 replaces stub persona prompt behavior with a governed PersonaComposer that reads Chirality instruction-root materials and produces prompt context for the SDK-backed runtime path.
The slice value is making prompt composition deterministic, traceable, source-grounded, and bounded by Chirality-owned runtime policy.
Chirality owns the prompt contract; SDK defaults, transcript shape, vendor assumptions, or ambient settings must not decide PersonaComposer behavior.
The instruction root is read authority, not a runtime write target; ordinary project execution must not mutate governance or AGENT_<persona>.md files.
Prompt text supports policy but does not enforce it; enforcement relies on SDK options, denied tools, hooks, canUseTool, path policy, and Chirality overlays.

Fingerprints should reflect real inputs: persona content, governance preface, mode, tool/policy inputs, settings-source posture, MCP server versions, and subagent policy version, not just persona name and mode.
Keep provider-specific terms behind the adapter boundary; public Chirality contracts and runtime events must remain provider-neutral.
Use docs/TYPES.md Section 3.4 for alias vocabulary unless a more specific accepted alias resolver exists by implementation time.
Treat the working-root summary as contextual prompt material, not as instruction-root governance and not as project-truth validation.
Keep prompt assembly deterministic with stable section ordering, stable omitted-field behavior, and explicit handling for missing optional inputs.
Prefer structured composer inputs over ad hoc strings so tests can isolate persona content, governance preface, mode, tool surface, and fingerprint material.
If DEL-04-02 owns the final SDK option/tool-surface object, this deliverable should accept that resolved surface rather than reconstruct it.

Resolve aliases locally only for the canonical docs/TYPES.md Section 3.4 vocabulary, or delegate when an accepted DEL-08-02 resolver/interface owns broader alias behavior; the decision criterion is ownership.
If DEL-08-01 or DEL-08-02 changes instruction-root packaging or alias contracts, update the composer through an explicit dependency note rather than local convention.

For prompt detail vs enforcement: include concise governance/mode/tool reminders but enforce with runtime policy, since long prompts can drift into false reliance if not backed by hooks and permissions.

For alias handling: handle source-defined mappings locally unless DEL-08-02 provides an accepted resolver returning canonical agent names and typed failures, since duplication risks divergence and over-delegation can obscure missing-persona failures.
For fingerprint breadth: hash real prompt and policy inputs that affect runtime behavior using stable normalized inputs, since broader fingerprints can churn on non-semantic metadata.
For SDK-specific names: keep them as adapter/tool metadata where necessary, since overexposure makes Chirality appear SDK-shaped and underexposure makes tool context unclear.
Final prompt template examples require accepted implementation interfaces for PersonaComposer inputs, resolved tool surface, working-root summary shape, and boot metadata shape.
ASSUMPTION: a useful test fixture varies one input at a time (agent instruction content, mode, visible tool list) and asserts the boot fingerprint changes for each supported input.

The procedure provides an operational path to implement and verify the PersonaComposer slice, replacing stub prompt behavior with deterministic source-grounded composition from instruction-root governance, active persona, working-root policy, mode, and permitted tool-surface inputs.
Prerequisite: the instruction root must be readable and contain required governance and agent resources.
Prerequisite: the working root must remain separate from the instruction root and provide contextual project-root information only.
Prerequisite: use or delegate the accepted persona alias mappings from docs/TYPES.md Section 3.4.
Prerequisite: use resolved mode and permitted tool-surface inputs supplied by the runtime/options layer.

Prerequisite: extracted ACTIVE upstream edges identify DEL-04-02 for mode/tool-surface inputs, DEL-08-01 for instruction-root packaging/conformance, DEL-08-02 for alias routing/resolver, and a PRD source-snapshot constraint.

Step 1: confirm target boundaries so the implementation stays in the prompt/persona composition slice and does not absorb SDK option building, Provider/SDK message mapping, provider key/network handling, or instruction-root packaging conformance.

Step 2: define PersonaComposer inputs including selected persona, project root or working-root summary, mode, permitted tool surface, governance preface source, persona instruction content source, and available fingerprint-policy inputs; preserve unresolved fields as explicit optional/TBD inputs.

Step 3: resolve persona identity by normalizing aliases or delegating to the accepted resolver and resolving the canonical persona to agents/AGENT_<persona>.md; missing persona should produce a typed failure.
The exact missing-persona token PERSONA_NOT_FOUND is PRD-derived and requires confirmation against an accepted PRD snapshot.

Step 4: read required governance preface and selected agent instruction content from the instruction root; do not write to it, and preserve instruction-root path protection as runtime policy, not prompt convention.

Step 5: compose prompt material deterministically as a stable ordered prompt from governance preface, persona instruction, working-root boundary/summary, mode policy, permitted tool surface, and professional-boundary reminders, omitting unavailable optional sections in a documented stable way.

Step 6: preserve policy boundaries so prompt text describes mode/tool posture but does not enforce permissions; enforcement remains with SDK options, denied tools, canUseTool, hooks, path containment, and Chirality overlays.

Step 7: produce boot fingerprint inputs by normalizing and hashing supported inputs such as persona content, governance preface, mode, visible SDK tool names/versions, permission-policy version, settings-source posture, MCP server versions, and subagent policy version, recording unavailable inputs as TBD.

Step 8: integrate with the runtime boundary by passing composed prompt material and fingerprint metadata to the product-owned runtime boundary without making public APIs, UIEvent, HarnessEvent, or session storage SDK-shaped.

Step 9: add persona content hash tests, fingerprint sensitivity tests, missing persona tests, alias or resolver-delegation tests, prompt section inclusion tests, and checks that API keys/transcripts/local presets do not become prompt authority.

Step 10: record unresolved dependencies on DEL-04-02 tool-surface shape, DEL-08-01 instruction-root integrity, or DEL-08-02 alias routing explicitly for extraction rather than encoding a silent local assumption.

The Specification covers the backend PersonaComposer slice replacing stub prompt behavior with source-grounded composition from instruction-root governance, active persona, working-root policy, current mode, and permitted tool surface.
Included: resolve selected and alias-normalized persona names to instruction-root agents/AGENT_<persona>.md content.
Included: compose prompt material from governance preface, selected agent instruction, working-root summary, mode policy, permitted tool surface, and professional-boundary reminders.
Included: preserve instruction-root/working-root separation and product-owned runtime semantics.
Included: provide boot fingerprint inputs that reflect actual prompt and SDK-policy material.
Excluded: SDK option construction, settingSources: [], and tool list construction beyond accepting the configured permitted tool surface; these belong primarily to DEL-04-02.
Excluded: SDK stream/message translation, which belongs to DEL-04-03.
Excluded: API key, base URL, network policy, and provider error classification, which belong to DEL-04-05.
Excluded: instruction-root packaging conformance beyond consuming readable files, which belongs primarily to DEL-08-01 and DEL-09-04.
PC-REQ-001: the composer MUST consume a validated instruction root containing required governance and agent resources before reading persona content.
PC-REQ-002: the composer MUST NOT write to the instruction root during ordinary runtime execution.
PC-REQ-003: the composer MUST preserve instruction-root and working-root separation; working-root content must not be treated as instruction-root governance.
PC-REQ-004: persona names MUST resolve to canonical agents/AGENT_<persona>.md files; missing-persona handling is PERSONA_NOT_FOUND per PRD, subject to the REF-006 hash warning.
PC-REQ-005: persona aliases SHOULD use the canonical docs/TYPES.md Section 3.4 mappings before instruction-file lookup, or delegate to an accepted resolver implementing those mappings.
PC-REQ-006: the composed prompt MUST include selected agent instruction content, global/governance context, working-root boundaries, mode policy, and the configured permitted tool surface.
PC-REQ-007: the composed prompt MUST include professional-boundary reminders and MUST NOT imply autonomous professional approval, certification, signing, sealing, issuing, or external validation.
PC-REQ-008: prompt text MUST NOT be treated as the enforcement boundary for filesystem writes, tool exposure, bash, subagents, or domain operations.

PC-REQ-009: the composer MUST keep Chirality contracts provider-neutral; SDK names, transcript paths, and permission modes may appear only as adapter metadata or prompt support, not as public contract definitions.

PC-REQ-010: boot fingerprints SHOULD include persona content hash, governance preface hash, mode, SDK tool names/versions, permission-policy version, settings-source posture, MCP server versions, and subagent policy version when available; adjacent unresolved inputs remain TBD.
PC-REQ-011: unknown runtime option keys relevant to composition MUST be ignored with warnings rather than silently mutating prompt behavior.

PC-REQ-012: the composer MUST treat SDK transcripts, chat drafts, local presets, model context, API keys, and runtime caches as non-authoritative unless imported through a governed project-file process.
Standard: the instruction-root contract requires required resources, read-only ordinary execution, and integrity expectations.
Standard: composer output feeds a product-owned runtime engine boundary, not SDK-shaped public semantics.
Standard: runtime options and persona composition define fallback chains and prompt composition ingredients.
Standard: prompt content may describe mode/tool posture, but runtime restrictions require code-level enforcement.
Standard: the persona alias vocabulary defines the canonical UI-alias-to-agent mapping.
Verification PC-REQ-001 through PC-REQ-005: unit tests for instruction-root validation, canonical persona path resolution, alias mapping or resolver delegation, and missing-persona behavior.
Verification PC-REQ-006 through PC-REQ-009: snapshot or structured-content tests proving the composed prompt includes required sections while avoiding SDK-shaped public contracts.

Verification PC-REQ-011: runtime option tests proving unknown composition-related option keys warn and do not mutate prompt behavior.
Verification PC-REQ-012: tests or review checks proving API keys, SDK transcripts, local presets, and draft chat state are not imported into prompt authority or project truth.
